title: Lake water is densest a few degrees above freezing, so the coldest water stays on top
summary: Near 4 degrees Celsius, lake water is denser than water at the freezing point, so the colder surface water stays up instead of sinking.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says water at about 39 degrees Fahrenheit, which it also writes as 4 degrees Celsius, is denser than water at 32 degrees Fahrenheit, the freezing point. In lakes, the denser water sinks below less-dense water. If water were densest at the freezing point, the very cold surface water would sink and a lake could freeze from the bottom up. The page says water's heat capacity makes it a good insulator, so some lakes frozen that way might not fully thaw in summer. This is the Survey's account of ordinary lakes. It is not a forecast for a named lake, and the degree table is not copied.
